evidence: Assigned-row source review passes. Workbook Quality Checks row 37 (number 36), matching Internal Quality Checks row 37, and frozen quality-checks.md:149-151 require mutation probes to be absent from seed/reference initial state. This is a bounded source check, not an execution of the private check-probe-not-in-seed.py checker. Within the frozen task, tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:11 requires unique identifiers with a per-session suffix, excludes earlier judges' records as controls, and requires dedicated requisitions. P1 at :28 and P4 at :34 prescribe the distinct ID patterns " req /?# <suffix> ", " offer /?# <suffix> ", " chain req /?# <suffix> ", and " chain offer /?# <suffix> ". A read-only Python literal scan found zero occurrences of all four static stems in every solution file and the public seed. The public and reference seeds are byte-identical, SHA256 1b39015461a7a4f23b835aeea9584caffd0266c64d394778376cbd6c8a18bcf7, with only seven REQ-* requisitions and thirteen OFF-* offers; neither contains new probe identities or revision lineages. solution/app/src/db.js:122-179 initializes solely from that roster and creates only the SEEDED/roster loaded audit entry; solution/solve.sh installs a fresh disposable database baseline. The frozen task contains no .db/.sqlite artifact. Initial markup at solution/app/public/index.html:1-56 has no mutation records; dynamic form defaults at public/js/hireops.js:62-65 and :205-218 are ordinary REQ-NEW-1/OFF-NEW-1/New Requisition/New Candidate values, none mandated as judge probes. A date, amount, actor or referrer shared with the seed is not being used as a unique mutation witness: operations and readbacks are bound to the newly saved identity. OFF-DC is deliberately a seeded PENDING self-approval target, not a promised fresh creation; tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:326 requires its actual refusal followed by distinct-approver success on the same target. The creation gate at tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:23-26 requires uniquely named new records and exact independent Auditor readback; functional judge.toml:785-794 requires fresh writes for readback/restart, expressly excluding a seeded-only substitute. Polish prompt.md:8 requires unique Polish-owned records and judge.toml:95-113 requires distinctive entered/changed field values, preventing unchanged defaults from proving recovery. Adversarial check considered a no-op create handler returning HTTP200 while leaving only the seed visible: it cannot satisfy new-identity readback. Existing supplementary browser evidence confirms this bounded witness: local/gate-witness/results.json reports no_op_create reqSaved=false, offerSaved=false, freshReq=false, freshOffer=false and basic_gate_observations_satisfied=false despite status200, while golden has the corresponding saved/readback facts true. Verified results hash fd8410bc91102874ef98edfdbacf19f7853687956e076acc684d36c565d9ec75, driver hash 3c29a86eafb72caf23445c14850704878e5353fa2c9fb7ecf5903feaa0f197fc and no-op log hash ddbd3af2956a1be860c8b0d8ba101a6629958d473609fef7cbaf723de879b929 against raw-evidence-index.json; the twelve relevant frozen seed/reference/prompt/judge file hashes also match its gate-witness source binding. This is scripted local evidence, not a configured-judge score. Conforming-alternative check: an implementation may expose differently formatted dates/currency and its own generated successor IDs; these do not fail the probe because functional prompt.md:11 allows schema/label/ID-format variation and gate judge.toml:24 accepts equivalent money/date representations while retaining exact caller-chosen identity.
